ch15.anchor: till he reaches the Yellow River
ch15.note: From the proverb 'his heart won't die till he reaches the Yellow River' (不到黄河心不死): a man who will not give up a fixed purpose until he runs up against an absolute, undeniable barrier.

ch15.anchor: the weight of a thousand jun
ch15.note: The jun (钧) was an old unit of weight of about thirty catties (very roughly fifteen kilograms); 'a thousand jun' is a stock figure for a crushing, decisive weight—as in the idiom of a thousand-jun load hung by a single hair.

Wang Zhaoming (汪兆铭) was Wang Jingwei's real given name; 'Jingwei,' the name he is known by, was his pen name. Official documents and formal records—like the ones quoted here—call him Wang Zhaoming, so the assassination target and 'Wang Jingwei' are one and the same man.

The French street-name of Wang Jingwei's residence in colonial Hanoi; the same house Chen elsewhere calls by its Chinese name, Gao Lang Street. Hanoi being French-ruled, its streets carried French names.

Zhu Zhixin (朱执信, 1885–1920), an early revolutionary theorist and one of Sun Yat-sen's closest comrades in the Tongmenghui, killed by warlord troops in 1920 and revered thereafter as a martyr of the republican cause. To be his daughter is to come of impeccable revolutionary stock.

ch15.anchor: into the very wood three-tenths of an inch deep
ch15.note: The idiom ru mu san fen (入木三分): the brush-strokes of the great calligrapher Wang Xizhi were said to have soaked three-tenths of an inch into the wooden board beneath the paper—hence writing, or insight, that is penetratingly incisive and cuts to the quick.
